clue.text: Very attentive humorist visiting too briefly

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's home, so one piece sits within the other
cut short, so the last letter of the word for too is dropped

parts.note: too means as well, also
Edward Lear, writer of nonsense verse and limericks

explanation.surface: A comedian dropping in for a short stay keeps everyone hanging on his every word.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear, the Victorian limerick writer, is a stock crossword humorist; briefly trims only the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is all ears is listening eagerly, an idiom for close and keen attention.

clue.text: Bogie's mate's playing unknown song

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being played about with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, both possessive esses included
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Humphrey Bogart's friend Sam plays a piano tune whose name we are not told.
explanation.walkthrough: Bogie is Humphrey Bogart, and in Casablanca his friend Sam is asked to play exactly this song, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous standard sung by Dooley Wilson in Casablanca, so it is a song by example.

clue.text: Motorboat to slide into water

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large powered pleasure boat
second meaning: to set a newly built vessel afloat

explanation.surface: Someone eases a speedboat down the slipway into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a big motor-driven boat, and the verb means setting a ship afloat for the first time.

clue.text: Star student refurbished Oslo garret

indicators.note: a refurbished room has been done up and its contents rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A top pupil does up an attic flat in the Norwegian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Star student looks like a brilliant pupil, but it means someone who studies the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer reads meaning into planets and constellations, a whimsical way of being a student of stars.

clue.text: Tree French Nobelist Albert climbs

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Albert Camus, French writer who won the Nobel Prize for Literature

explanation.surface: The French author Albert Camus scrambles up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree with red autumn leaves and berries used as a spice.

clue.text: Sorry American hiding in an outhouse

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is concealed inside it

parts.note: a shed is a small outbuilding
AM is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A shamefaced American has gone to ground in a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorry in the sense of embarrassed regret is being ashamed of what one did.

clue.text: Without piano, a top jazz singer unaccompanied

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other pieces surround this one

parts.note: taken as written
a cap is a lid or top
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A star jazz vocalist performs with no pianist to back her.
explanation.walkthrough: Without reads as lacking, which fits the surface, but here it has its old sense of outside, so the piano sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing a cappella means performing with voices alone, with no instrumental backing at all.

clue.text: Warm through hearts: enjoy meal

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
to eat is to enjoy a meal

explanation.surface: A romantic dinner leaves two lovers glowing inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat food is to warm it all the way through before serving, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Redesigned Armenian national symbol

indicators.note: something redesigned has been reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Armenia gets a fresh emblem for the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Armenia, but the symbol belongs to France.
explanation.definitionFit: Marianne, the woman in a Phrygian cap, personifies the French Republic on stamps and coins.

clue.text: Song writer initially lodged with the Crawleys?

indicators.note: a lodger lives inside another family's house, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Crawleys are the aristocratic family of Downton Abbey, the British TV period drama

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of writer

explanation.surface: A songwriter boards with the aristocratic family from the TV drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the Crawleys stand for their house, Downton, by association.
explanation.definitionFit: Downtown is the 1964 hit sung by Petula Clark, so the song is defined by example.

clue.text: Confidence in being tied up, do we hear?

indicators.note: asks whether we hear it, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: trussed means bound up with rope

explanation.surface: A question of whether faith survives being bound hand and foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust is firm belief in someone's reliability, so it is a close synonym for confidence.

clue.text: Actress reversing target initially fired dart

indicators.note: reversing means the word for target is read backwards

parts.note: an aim is a target

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: first letter of fired
a dart is a small arrow-like missile

explanation.surface: An actress backs away from the dartboard after a first throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Mia Farrow is the American film actress of Rosemary's Baby fame, named by example.

clue.text: Composer worried about case of Icelandic instrument

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the other piece
worried in the sense of tugged about and disturbed, so the letters get disordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so only the outer letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Icelandic

explanation.surface: A composer frets over a set of Icelandic musical instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Composer and instrument both point to music, but the instrument is a scientific one.
explanation.definitionFit: A microscope is a laboratory instrument for magnifying tiny objects, a scientific rather than musical tool.

clue.text: Large, having devoured seconds? Restrict diet

indicators.note: whatever is devoured ends up inside the eater

parts.note: fat means large in girth
s is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A big eater who went back for second helpings is told to cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: Seconds suggests extra helpings of food; it is the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food, or limit eating, for a period, which is restricting one's diet.

clue.text: Sweet Starmer embraces every one on island

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed on top of what follows
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: Keir Starmer is Prime Minister, PM
each means every one
Elba is the Italian island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister hugs everyone he meets while visiting an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the UK Prime Minister, so he stands for PM; sweet is the British word for a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach Melba is a dessert of peaches, ice cream and raspberry sauce, and a sweet is a pudding course.

clue.text: Possibly follow Karen with song she recorded?

indicators.note: possibly marks one of several possible arrangements of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
w is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A fan of Karen Carpenter might go after one of her records.
explanation.walkthrough: Karen is Karen Carpenter of the Carpenters, who had a hit with this song in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carpenters' recording of this ballad was sung by Karen, so it is a song she recorded.

clue.text: Love helping after fuss

indicators.note: after places the first named piece behind the second one

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: Affection offered as a helping hand after a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship, a strong synonym for intense affection.

clue.text: Set with fault corrected: that's pleasing

indicators.note: something corrected has been put right, rearranged into proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is glad that a defect in a piece of equipment has been put right.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteful means showing good aesthetic judgment, so pleasing to the eye or sense of style.

clue.text: Clear detective set task to protect copyright

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a stint is an allotted spell of work
c is the symbol for copyright

explanation.surface: A police inspector is assigned to guard someone's intellectual property.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct means plainly visible or easy to perceive, so it is a synonym for clear.

clue.text: Meanie Franco's discordant song

indicators.note: discordant means jarring and out of harmony, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited man called Franco sings a harsh, tuneless number.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fine Romance is the Jerome Kern standard sung by Fred Astaire, so a song by example.

clue.text: In French, with heart, play it again

parts.note: en is the French word for in
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: A French audience passionately calls for a repeat performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Encore is the cry from an audience demanding a repeat, effectively asking the performer to do it once more.

clue.text: See 1
Farewell from Indian steel producer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal British goodbye
second meaning: the Indian industrial group that owns ... Steel

explanation.surface: An Indian steelmaker says goodbye, perhaps to a British plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a casual British way of saying goodbye, and the Tata conglomerate makes steel.

clue.text: City a study in distressed stone

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
distressed furniture is deliberately battered, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
to cram is to study hard

explanation.surface: A city is portrayed as a sculpture study carved in weathered stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California, so it is a city named by example.

clue.text: Despicable type news boss admired

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor admired someone who turned out to be a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rated in informal use means esteemed or thought highly of, as in a player who is highly rated.

clue.text: Asian location covered in cruciverbalists

indicators.note: something covered in a word is concealed within its letters

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: An Asian holiday spot overrun with crossword fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island, so it is a place in Asia named by example.

clue.text: Duke retaining soldier as space cadet?

indicators.note: retaining something means holding it inside

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, as in put up your dukes
a soldier is a caste of ant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman keeps a trooper on his staff as an astronaut trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke and soldier suggest rank and army; duke is slang for fist and the soldier is an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A space cadet is someone with their head in the clouds, a dreamer who lives in fantasy.

clue.text: Searches for beauty

explanation.surface: Someone goes hunting for something beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Looks for is a phrasal verb meaning hunts or seeks, and good looks are physical attractiveness.

clue.text: European fixer back to instal a telly

indicators.note: installing something puts it in place inside, so one piece goes within the other
back means the word for fixer is read backwards

parts.note: a nail fixes things together
taken as written
telly is British slang for television, TV

explanation.surface: A handyman from Europe comes back to set up a television.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latvian is a native of Latvia, one of the Baltic states, so a European by example.

clue.text: Year-end frolics in clergyman's office

indicators.note: frolics are playful romps, so the letters skip about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: End-of-year office party high jinks in a vicar's study.
explanation.definitionFit: A deanery is the official residence or position of a dean, a senior cleric.
